newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian cotton prices eased on fresh state offers.
newsitem.headline: Indian cotton prices eased on fresh state offers.

text.p: Indian cotton prices fell on Monday on sluggish overseas enquiries as well as fresh supplies from state agencies, dealers said.
"Mill buying was also low while improved new crop arrivals dragged down prices," one dealer said.
Last week's crop arrivals fell due to cold weather which has now improved and also seen more crops coming in, dealers said.
In spot deals Bengal-deshi slid by 15/20 rupees to 790/850 rupees per maund (37.32 kg) while Punjab saw-ginned fell by 5/15 rupees to 1,410/1,620 rupees per maund.
F-414 fell by 15 rupees to 1,835/1,865 rupees per maund. Gujarat cotton however moved in a narrow range and finished on a quiet note.
